passage: Urban planners are increasingly turning to predictive analytics to improve city transportation systems. Instead of relying solely on historical data or manual traffic counts, modern models continuously incorporate live information from sensors, navigation apps, and public transit networks. These tools allow planners to forecast congestion hours in advance and evaluate the potential impact of proposed changes, such as adjusting bus routes or modifying traffic light timing. One of the major advantages of predictive analytics is its ability to test multiple scenarios before any physical changes occur, reducing both cost and risk. However, the effectiveness of these models depends heavily on the quality of the data they receive. Inaccurate or incomplete inputs can lead to flawed predictions, potentially worsening traffic patterns rather than improving them. Despite these challenges, cities adopting data-driven planning have seen notable improvements in commute times, public transit reliability, and overall urban mobility.
